# Phase Three — Final Critique and Thirty Additional Improvements

The Awtsmoos asks the plan to stand trial before a single source file is stirred;
Awtsmoos.com must prove the architecture can survive reload, mobile fingers, comments, and every remembered word.

## What phase two still risked

The previous plan could still over-assume the shape of the Tanach corpus. The repository has a Torah Library bookshelf but the actual rich post reader may use a separate canonical post model. Therefore the generic reference contract must be adapter-driven and must not hard-code Wikisource page IDs. Chitas can initially use whichever internal Tanach adapter the real reader already uses, while the abstraction remains capable of supporting ordinary post ranges.

## Thirty-plus additional corrections

1. Do not implement source resolution until the exact reader entry module and internal Tanach payload are read.
2. If Tanach text is already ordinary Heichel posts, prefer `post-range` references first.
3. If Tanach has a specialized API, keep it behind `tanach-range` adapter.
4. The generic contract should allow multiple source kinds without optional-field soup.
5. Validate ranges on creation and again on resolution.
6. Canonical IDs must be deterministic across language changes.
7. Dynamic post IDs must never contain raw translated book names.
8. A Chitas card description may show the reference but must not be the reader body source.
9. Week selection must update both list and opened dynamic post coherently.
10. Reader language toggle must not accidentally shift to another calendar week.
11. Date picker must accept any civil date, then derive its Sunday week anchor.
12. Hebrew labels should include Hebrew weekday/parsha names where metadata exists.
13. English mode should preserve Hebrew title as secondary context, not erase it.
14. Directionality must be scoped to Torah text, not flip the global navigation chrome.
15. Reader typography should inherit native Tanach tokens before adding Chitas accents.
16. Do not create an iframe or duplicate scroll container.
17. Bottom mobile dock must not cover the final verse or comment composer.
18. Reader masthead controls must wrap cleanly at 320px.
19. All buttons/selectors must have accessible labels and at least 44px, preferably 48px, hit size.
20. Week navigation should work with keyboard as well as touch.
21. Preserve browser back/forward semantics when changing week/date.
22. If controls use `history.pushState`, popstate must reconstruct state.
23. Avoid fetching seven full Torah ranges just to display seven list cards; resolve full text only after opening one post.
24. List cards should remain lightweight schedule metadata.
25. Reader post resolution should fetch only the selected range.
26. Comments count on list cards may stay lazy; comments UI must load on reader.
27. Stable dynamic post thread identity should include date when the same canonical range can recur in different Chitas contexts, unless product semantics explicitly want one shared thread.
28. Verse-level comments should always map back to canonical source identity so Torah discussion can be reused.
29. Unit tests should distinguish thread identity from source identity.
30. Simchas Torah special references need explicit adapter rules because phrases like “through the end” are not ordinary fixed strings.
31. Isru Chag “from beginning through portion” requires a cumulative Bereishis range, not just a display sentence.
32. Festival-deferral behavior must be tested with actual internal range construction.
33. If source resolution cannot map a book alias, error internally with useful context rather than redirect externally.
34. No code path should mention `chabad.org` after migration, except historical docs/tests if explicitly retained.
35. Search the changed subtree for `externalHref`, `virtualStudy`, and Chabad host before completion.
36. Search for generic card vertical decorative labels that can collide on mobile; Chitas custom layout should avoid them.
37. Preserve ordinary Living Path grouping behavior and owner controls.
38. Dynamic posts are read-only compositions unless a future explicit persistence flow is built.
39. Do not let edit/delete governance controls appear on virtual dynamic Chitas posts.
40. Do let social/comment/share controls appear where ordinary read-only posts permit them.
41. Add a resolver provenance field for debugging, but do not expose internal implementation noise to ordinary users.
42. Add concise internal loading skeleton rather than the large fallback panel shown in the screenshot.
43. Verify no CLS/scroll jump when text resolves.
44. Verify selected language and date persist after hard reload.
45. Verify selecting another week while a post is open gives a predictable reader/list transition.

## Final architecture after critique

The generic dynamic-reference layer defines identity and composition but knows nothing about calendars. A source registry chooses internal adapters. Chitas is a producer: schedule metadata becomes canonical range references only when a particular day is opened. Living Path list cards remain light native posts. The existing reader remains the presentation/social owner. Chitas contributes a masthead and week-state controls, not a parallel reader.

This is the least magical architecture: every behavior can be reconstructed from URL + canonical source + schedule metadata, and every comment or progress marker has an explicit stable identity.
